app.title: TerraLens — Earth System Trend Detective
ctrl.ceres.title: 2001 sensor filter
ctrl.ceres.help: Restrict solar irradiance to the homogeneous CERES era (2001 onwards).
ctrl.extremes.title: Remove extreme months
ctrl.extremes.help: Recompute the trend without the months flagged as multivariate anomalies.
ctrl.csv.help: Download the monthly series as CSV
alert.network: The server could not be reached. Check that TerraLens is running. {message}
alert.rateLimited: Too many requests in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.
viewGuide.tab-trends: Is the change real? Two trend lines, the largest level shift and corrections for month-to-month memory.
viewGuide.tab-ml: Which months were unusual, and what explains soil moisture? Three anomaly detectors and a Random Forest checked against persistence.
viewGuide.tab-acker: Does the trend survive without the extreme months? The outlier test of Acker et al. (2009) for every variable.
viewGuide.tab-dipole: Do two regions respond to El Niño in opposite ways, and do their trends differ?
viewGuide.tab-multiscale: Trends on the ~55 km grid over Ecuador, MODIS vegetation, 1 km model snapshots and a probe for any coordinate.
viewGuide.tab-telemetry: How well do the machine-learning models do on years they never saw, compared with simple persistence?
viewGuide.tab-guide: What each control and correction does.
viewGuide.tab-about: The problem, the method, the data and the limits.
answer.sig_increase: In {region}, {variable} rises {slope} {units} ({from}–{to}). The trend is real: it holds after correcting for month-to-month memory ({p}).
answer.sig_decrease: In {region}, {variable} falls {slope} {units} ({from}–{to}). The trend is real: it holds after correcting for month-to-month memory ({p}).
answer.marginal_increase: In {region}, {variable} may be rising ({slope} {units}, {from}–{to}), but the evidence is weak ({p}).
answer.marginal_decrease: In {region}, {variable} may be falling ({slope} {units}, {from}–{to}), but the evidence is weak ({p}).
answer.not_significant: In {region}, {variable} shows no reliable trend in {from}–{to} ({p}); the changes stay within natural variability.
answer.autocorr_rejected: In {region}, {variable} appears to change {slope} {units}, but month-to-month memory explains it: after correction the trend is not reliable.
warning.step_dominated: Looks like one step around {date} rather than a gradual trend: check whether the data changed.
warning.known_splice_in_window: The series crosses the documented source change of {splice} (step {delta} {units}). Turn on the 2001 filter.
warning.start_moved: For this variable the analysis starts in {year}.
shape.step: A single step fits better than a trend (ΔBIC {dbic}).
shape.trend: A gradual trend fits better than a step (ΔBIC {dbic}).
shape.inconclusive: Step and trend fit about equally well (ΔBIC {dbic}).
trends.monthly.subtitle: Monthly anomalies (value minus that month's normal) with two trend lines and the largest level shift
trends.annual.title: Annual means
trends.annual.subtitle: Averaging each year removes most month-to-month memory
trends.scan.title: All six variables at once
trends.scan.subtitle: Testing six variables raises the chance of a false alarm, so q-values control the false discovery rate. Click a row to open that variable.
trends.clim.title: Normal year (mean ± 1σ per month)
trends.clim.subtitle: The seasonal cycle removed before looking for trends
trends.seasonal.title: Trend by season
trends.seasonal.subtitle: Which season drives the change (December counts with the following January–February)
scan.coincident: {n} variables ({variables}) shift within two months of {date}. A shift shared by several variables can come from a change in the input data; check before trusting their trends.
ml.pca.title: Months in two dimensions (PCA) and regimes
ml.pca.variance: PC1 explains {pc1}% and PC2 {pc2}% of the variance · {k} regimes chosen by silhouette score
ml.rf.title: What explains root-zone soil moisture?
ml.rf.subtitle: Random Forest on this month's and earlier rainfall, temperature, humidity, radiation and ENSO
ml.rf.insightBeats: The most predictive input is {feature}. Out of sample the model explains R² = {cv}, more than persistence alone ({persistence}).
ml.rf.insightLoses: The most predictive input is {feature}, but out of sample the model (R² = {cv}) does worse than simply assuming next month repeats this one ({persistence}). Read the ranking as association, not prediction.
ml.rf.unavailable: Not enough soil-moisture data to fit the model here.
ml.anomalies.title: Months that at least two of three detectors call unusual
ml.anomalies.subtitle: Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor and Mahalanobis distance, each with its own data-driven threshold
ml.anomalies.none: No month is flagged by two detectors in this region.
acker.chart.title: Trend with and without the anomalous months
acker.chart.subtitle: Per decade, full period of each variable
acker.table.title: Outlier test (Acker et al., 2009)
acker.subtitle: Trends recomputed without the {n} months that at least two detectors flag
dipole.title: Compare two regions
dipole.subtitle: Standardized anomalies of both regions next to the ENSO index. Correlations use an effective sample size that accounts for month-to-month memory.
dipole.strongEnso: During strong ENSO months: r {r} ({n} months)
relation.enso.not_both_significant: No clear ENSO response in both
relation.trend.opposite: Long-term trends go in opposite directions
relation.trend.same_direction: Long-term trends go the same way
relation.trend.not_both_significant: Long-term trends are not both significant
map.title: Trend map over Ecuador (NASA POWER grid, ~55 km cells)
map.subtitle: Solid cells stay significant after controlling the false discovery rate across all cells. Pins are the benchmark regions.
map.aria: Map of trends per grid cell over Ecuador
modis.title: Vegetation (NDVI) — {region}, {n} images
modis.subtitle: 16-day NDVI from Terra/Aqua MODIS (MOD13Q1, 250 m), a single pixel at the region's point
modis.fallback: No MODIS series is cached for {region}; showing {fallback}.
mm.title: 1 km model snapshots (Meteomatics, 2023–2024)
mm.subtitle: One day every 10 days from a commercial downscaled model; not observations and not monthly means
stac.title: Data provenance: MODIS granules
stac.subtitle: Granules of the modis-13Q1-061 collection that contain the point (Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC)
stac.none: No granule metadata cached for this point.
probe.title: Check any coordinate
probe.subtitle: Downloads NASA POWER for a point and runs the same trend tests
probe.idle: Enter coordinates or turn on probe mode and click the map.
telemetry.intro: These benchmarks come from train_models.py, run offline. Every model is compared with persistence: predicting that next month repeats this month's anomaly. A model is only useful where it beats that baseline.
telemetry.missing: No benchmark manifest found. Run python train_models.py.
telemetry.nowcast.title: Nowcast over the Ecuador grid
telemetry.nowcast.subtitle: Uses same-month weather, so it explains the present rather than predicting the future
telemetry.perm.title: What the best nowcast relies on
telemetry.perm.subtitle: Drop in test R² when each input is shuffled
telemetry.forecast.title: Forecast: only data known in advance
telemetry.forecast.subtitle: Predicting soil moisture 1 and 3 months ahead
telemetry.regional.title: Regional driver models
telemetry.regional.subtitle: The model behind "What explains root-zone soil moisture?", per region. Negative R² means worse than predicting the average.
